suggestions.reason: As drafted, the clause states only that Consultant "accepts" the engagement without imposing an express contractual obligation to perform, which weakens the City of Westwood's ability to enforce performance and seek remedies if Consultant fails to deliver. Additionally, the phrase "services described in this Agreement" is undefined and unanchored, creating a material ambiguity about the scope of work that a court could not resolve without extrinsic evidence, exposing the City to scope disputes or Consultant claims of broader entitlement. Capitalizing and defining "Services" in this foundational provision establishes a precise, enforceable scope reference that flows consistently throughout the Agreement and strengthens the City's position in any performance or payment dispute.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement and Consultant accepts that engagement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement (the "Services"), and Consultant accepts that engagement and shall perform the Services in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause references Exhibit A for the scope of Contract Services but neither names the services in the body of the Agreement nor expressly identifies what falls outside that scope, creating two concrete risks for the City of Westwood. First, the absence of an out-of-scope boundary means the Consultant could dispute whether a particular task is already included within the existing Contract Services, potentially undermining the City's ability to enforce the written amendment requirement and control costs. Second, without naming the service type in the operative clause itself, the City faces an enforcement gap if Exhibit A is later disputed, lost, or found incomplete, leaving no independent anchor in the Agreement to define what the Consultant is obligated to perform. The written supplemental agreement requirement is an important protection for the City and is preserved, but it is weakened if the baseline scope remains ambiguous.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those Investment Management Services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Any services not expressly described in Exhibit A are outside the scope of the Contract Services. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: Section 3 as drafted is a bare cross-reference to Exhibit A and contains no operative payment terms whatsoever, exposing the City of Westwood to material financial and legal risk. Without a stated payment due date, invoice process, fee-fixity confirmation, expense approval requirement, or invoice dispute right, the Consultant could assert that fees are open-ended, that all expenses are reimbursable as incurred, and that any failure to pay on demand constitutes a breach — leaving the City with no contractual basis to withhold, dispute, or contest an invoice. Because the clause is entirely silent on these mechanics, the City has no documented protection if the Consultant later claims implied interest on overdue amounts or unilaterally submits inflated invoices. The suggested fix introduces the minimum necessary operative terms to close these gaps while preserving the existing Exhibit A and Section 2 cross-references.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant the fixed fees specified in Exhibit A for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement. The Consultant shall submit invoices to the City on a monthly basis, and the City shall pay undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days following receipt. The City may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and disputed amounts shall be withheld pending resolution without constituting a breach. All reimbursable expenses are included within the compensation set forth in Exhibit A unless the City provides prior written approval for additional expenses, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the termination-for-cause right available to the City of Westwood contains no cure period, meaning a disputed or minor non-performance could trigger a contested termination without giving Consultant a defined opportunity to remedy, exposing the City to a wrongful-termination claim and service disruption. Additionally, the clause permits Consultant to terminate "at any time" upon sixty (60) days' notice—including before November 30, 2024—while the City's convenience termination right is restricted to on and after that date, creating an asymmetry that leaves the City without recourse if Consultant walks off the project during the early performance period. The survival provision is also narrow, covering only indemnity and insurance; payment obligations and confidentiality are unaddressed, creating a gap that could prejudice the City following termination.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time on and after November 30, 2024, upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant. The City may terminate this Agreement for cause at any time upon written notice to Consultant if Consultant fails to cure a material breach within thirty (30) days following written notice of such breach from the City. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the effective date of termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, upon sixty (60) days' written notice to the City. The provisions regarding indemnity, insurance, confidentiality, and payment for services rendered shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 6 exposes the City of Westwood to material compliance gaps: the clause is silent on bribery and corrupt practices, imposes no obligation on Consultant to notify the City when a legal violation occurs that affects this Agreement, fails to allocate responsibility for the cost of complying with changes in law enacted after commencement, and contains no supply-chain labor standards (e.g., prohibitions on forced or child labor). Without a notification obligation, the City of Westwood may learn of a compliance failure only after it has suffered reputational or legal harm; without a cost-allocation provision, Consultant could argue that mid-performance law changes excuse performance or entitle it to additional fees. The indemnity in the final sentence is unaffected and preserved in full.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with all local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement, including any changes thereto enacted during the term, at Consultant's sole cost, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Such compliance shall include prohibitions on bribery and corrupt practices and the taking of commercially reasonable steps to prevent forced or child labor in Consultant's supply chain in connection with the Contract Services. Consultant shall promptly notify the City in writing upon becoming aware of any violation of applicable law affecting this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause binds Consultant only to two Kansas equal opportunity statutes, leaving City of Westwood without contractual protection against bribery and corruption, supply chain labor violations (including forced labor and human trafficking), and—critically—without any obligation on Consultant to disclose a legal breach that could compromise the Agreement or expose the City to reputational or regulatory liability. Because the City is a public entity, any association with a Consultant engaged in corrupt practices or exploitative labor supply chains presents a direct financial, legal, and public accountability risk to City of Westwood. The absence of a breach-notification obligation further means the City could remain unaware of a Consultant violation until after damage has already occurred.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.), the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.), and all other applicable laws and regulations, including those governing anti-bribery and supply chain labor standards (including prohibitions on forced labor and human trafficking), and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant shall promptly notify City of Westwood in writing of any breach of applicable law or regulation that affects, or is reasonably likely to affect, Consultant's performance under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The insurance obligation currently runs only "throughout the duration of this Agreement," leaving City of Westwood exposed to uninsured claims arising from the Consultant's work that are first asserted after expiration or earlier termination—a common occurrence in professional services engagements where defects or errors surface well after project completion. Equally problematic, the clause is silent on whether the specified insurance limits cap the Consultant's overall liability; without an express non-limitation statement, the Consultant could argue that the City accepted those policy amounts as a ceiling on its recovery, materially undermining City of Westwood's ability to pursue full indemnification or damages for significant losses. Together, these gaps create both a coverage gap and a liability-cap ambiguity that are adverse to the City's financial and legal interests.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years following its expiration or earlier termination, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The insurance requirements set forth herein shall not be construed to limit or cap Consultant's liability to the City under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits two procedurally critical elements of claims handling: Consultant has no obligation to obtain the City of Westwood's prior written consent before settling a claim, exposing the City to adverse precedents or reputational harm from settlements it did not approve; and there is no reciprocal cooperation obligation or mitigation duty on the City, leaving an implied mitigation defense available to Consultant that could reduce the City's recovery. Additionally, the clause does not clarify whether this indemnity obligation survives or is carved out from any limitation of liability or damages exclusion elsewhere in the Agreement, meaning any general liability cap could be invoked by Consultant to curtail the indemnity and leave the City of Westwood under-compensated for covered losses.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, and notwithstanding any limitation of liability or exclusion of damages set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision. Consultant shall not settle any such claim without the City's prior written consent. The City shall reasonably cooperate with Consultant in the defense of any such claim and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate any losses subject to indemnification under this Section.

suggestions.reason: The savings clause stating that duties "shall remain as imposed by law" is ambiguous because it is reasonably susceptible to two conflicting readings: one that it merely preserves pre-existing statutory or common-law duties without creating new claims, and another that it effectively preserves a third party's right to sue the City of Westwood by reference to whatever obligations law may impose. This ambiguity undermines the core purpose of the no-third-party-beneficiary disclaimer and could expose the City of Westwood to third-party claims it expressly sought to preclude, particularly in the context of personal injury or property damage litigation arising from the Consultant's services. Without clarifying language, a court could use the savings clause as a hook to allow a third party to assert rights against the City of Westwood under or in connection with this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law, provided that nothing in this sentence shall be construed to create any right of action in any third party against City or Consultant under or in connection with this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes the City of Westwood to significant procedural and financial risk on multiple fronts. The absence of a governing law designation leaves the City vulnerable to disputes over which jurisdiction's law applies, while the phrase "free to take such steps as it deems necessary" effectively grants the Consultant unfettered authority to initiate proceedings in any forum of its choosing, including one geographically or legally inconvenient to the City. The negotiation obligation is stated in precatory terms ("should") with no defined timeframe, rendering it unenforceable as a condition precedent, and the clause contains no carve-out permitting the City to seek emergency or injunctive relief without first completing negotiations—a critical omission where the City may need urgent judicial intervention to protect public interests or infrastructure. These deficiencies, taken together, leave the City of Westwood without a reliable, predictable, or home-forum dispute resolution mechanism.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 11. Disputes. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the City is located. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement shall first be addressed by negotiations between the parties for no less than thirty (30) days. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, either party may submit the matter to a court of competent jurisdiction in the City of Westwood; provided, however, that either party may seek injunctive or emergency relief in any court of competent jurisdiction without first completing such negotiation period. Notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: The existing provision consists solely of an anti-collusion representation, leaving City of Westwood without any enforceable standard governing how the Services must be performed, any warranty of legal compliance, or any protection against third-party intellectual property claims arising from deliverables received by the City. Without a performance standard, City of Westwood has no contractual basis to require correction or re-performance if the Services are delivered incompetently or negligently. The complete absence of a breach remedy means that even if a violation is established, the Agreement is silent on the City's available recourse, potentially requiring costly litigation to recover fees or compel re-performance that should be a matter of express contractual right.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Contractor further represents and warrants that it shall perform the Services with professional skill and care, comply with all applicable laws in connection with the Services, and not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights; and upon written notice from City of Westwood of any breach of the foregoing warranties, Contractor shall promptly re-perform the deficient Services or, at City of Westwood's election, refund the fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation in this clause runs solely in favor of the City of Westwood against the Consultant, but the City of Westwood itself makes no corresponding representation of authority. This creates a material enforceability gap: in the event of a dispute, the Consultant could raise the City's failure to represent its own authority as grounds to challenge the validity or binding effect of the Agreement against the City of Westwood. Converting the clause to a mutual representation by both parties eliminates that gap and establishes a symmetrical, market-standard foundation for enforceability of the Agreement on both sides.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each Party has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The warranty standards in Section 13 rely on phrases such as "state of the art procedures and techniques" and "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field" that are neither defined in the Agreement nor objectively determinable, creating a material enforcement risk for the City of Westwood: if the Consultant's work is substandard, the Consultant could dispute whether any identified standard was actually breached. Compounding this, the clause imposes warranty obligations on the Consultant but provides no corresponding remedy for the City of Westwood — most critically, no express right to require re-performance of nonconforming work at no additional cost — leaving the City without a clear contractual basis to compel correction without resorting to general damages litigation. Anchoring the standard to what qualified professionals customarily practice in the relevant field, and inserting a minimal re-performance right, closes both gaps while preserving the clause's existing structure.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to or exceed the professional standards customarily practiced by qualified professionals providing similar services in the relevant field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge consistent with generally accepted procedures and techniques applicable to all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and shall possess the requisite expertise and comprehension of the required subject matter to provide these services. In the event of a breach of the foregoing warranties, Consultant shall, at no additional cost to the City of Westwood, promptly re-perform the nonconforming work or services to the standard required herein.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 14 creates material operational and financial risk for the City of Westwood by failing to address three critical gaps: (1) the City receives no prior notice of a proposed assignment, leaving it unaware that the entity performing services has changed until after the fact; (2) the clause is silent on whether Consultant remains liable following a permitted assignment, meaning the original contracting party could walk away from its obligations entirely; and (3) there is no provision addressing a change of control of Consultant—such as a merger or acquisition by a competitor or unqualified firm—which could force the City into a performance relationship with an entity it never vetted or approved. The current binding-on-successors language ("whether consented to or not") compounds this risk by potentially legitimizing unauthorized transfers without preserving the City's remedies against the original Consultant.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant, including through merger, acquisition, or change of control, without the prior written consent of the City. Consultant shall provide the City with prior written notice of any proposed assignment or change of control no less than thirty (30) days in advance. No assignment, whether consented to or not, shall relieve Consultant of its obligations hereunder. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The Notices clause sets out Columbia Capital Management's address but contains no mechanism by which either party may update its notice details. Without such a mechanism, City of Westwood risks sending formal notices—including notices of breach, termination, or indemnity claims—to an address that is no longer current, potentially invalidating those notices or causing the City to lose critical contractual rights through no fault of its own. This gap equally leaves the City without a clear procedure to update its own contact information should its designated representative or address change during the term of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice address or designated recipient by providing written notice of such change to the other party, which change shall become effective ten (10) days following receipt of such written notice.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 16 fails to address three elements that are material to City of Westwood's risk exposure: it does not confirm that Consultant controls the manner and means of performance (a core factor in any worker-classification challenge), it does not extend Consultant's financial responsibility to wages, costs, and benefits owed to Consultant's own personnel, and it contains no mutual limitation on the authority of either party to bind the other. If the City were drawn into an employment, agency, or tax liability dispute arising from Consultant's engagements, the absence of these provisions would materially weaken the City's position and could expose City of Westwood to unbudgeted payroll-tax, benefits, or vicarious-liability claims.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who retains sole control over the manner and means of performing its obligations hereunder. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all wages, costs, benefits, taxes, and withholdings required by law for Consultant and its personnel, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Neither party shall have the authority to bind the other party to any obligation or commitment. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 17 addresses only the City of Westwood's Kansas Cash-Basis Law payment obligations and appropriations-based relief, while omitting any requirement on the provider to comply with applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, or supply-chain labour standards laws, and imposing no obligation on either party to notify the other upon a breach of law that materially affects Agreement performance. This exposes the City of Westwood to reputational, regulatory, and legal risk if the provider engages in corrupt practices or uses forced or child labour in its supply chain without recourse or prior notice, particularly given the public-entity context in which the City operates. Without a notification obligation, the City of Westwood may remain unaware of a legal breach by the provider until material harm has already occurred, undermining its ability to exercise any termination or remedial rights available under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. Each party shall also comply with all applicable laws and regulations governing its performance under this Agreement, including anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and laws prohibiting forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking in its supply chain. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects performance under this Agreement. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The current governing law clause designates Kansas law but is silent on forum, pre-dispute resolution steps, continuity of performance, and emergency relief rights, leaving City of Westwood with no procedural framework if a dispute arises with the counterparty. Without a designated exclusive forum binding both parties, the City risks being dragged into inconvenient or hostile venues at the counterparty's election, increasing litigation costs and uncertainty for a public entity with fixed budget constraints. The absence of a pre-dispute negotiation period and a continued-performance obligation also means the counterparty could halt Services and immediately commence proceedings without first engaging in good-faith resolution, creating operational disruption for the City. Aligning this clause with the Agreement's termination and notice provisions will be necessary to give the dispute escalation mechanism practical effect.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 19. Governing Law and Disputes. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas. Prior to commencing formal proceedings, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through senior representative negotiation for a period of thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. Any unresolved dispute shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in the State of Kansas, to which both parties irrevocably consent to jurisdiction and venue. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek urgent injunctive or equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction without first completing the negotiation period. Both parties shall continue performing their respective obligations under this Agreement during any pending dispute resolution process.

suggestions.reason: The second sentence of Section 21 states that capitalization "shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation" of terms throughout the Agreement, but it contains no carve-out for formally defined terms. This creates a material ambiguity for the City of Westwood: a counterparty or court could invoke this language to argue that capitalized Defined Terms — such as "Services," "Agreement," or "City" — carry no special interpretive weight, potentially eroding the specific, negotiated meanings on which City of Westwood's rights and protections depend. Left unaddressed, this provision could be weaponized to dilute defined-term precision at the moment of a dispute, undermining the City's ability to enforce key contractual obligations and limitations.
suggestions.original_text: Section 21. Descriptive Headings and Capitalization. The descriptive headings of the provisions of this Agreement are formulated and used only for convenience and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning and construction of any such provision. Some terms are capitalized throughout the Agreement, but use of or failure to use capitals shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation of such terms.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 21. Descriptive Headings and Capitalization. The descriptive headings of the provisions of this Agreement are formulated and used only for convenience and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning and construction of any such provision. Some terms are capitalized throughout the Agreement, but use of or failure to use capitals shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation of such terms; provided, however, that this sentence shall not affect the defined meaning of any term expressly defined in this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is legally uncertain on two fronts: courts do not automatically rewrite contract provisions, and "all applicable legal requirements" is an untethered standard that does not anchor any reformation to the parties' original bargain. For City of Westwood, this creates a material risk that a counterparty could assert that an invalid provision has been reformed in a manner favorable to the counterparty and adverse to the City, with no agreed standard to constrain the outcome. Without a minimum-change and original-intent standard, City of Westwood has no contractual basis to resist a reformulated provision that imposes materially different or more burdensome obligations than those originally negotiated.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall be reformed and amended to the minimum extent necessary to render it valid and enforceable, consistent with the original intent of the parties, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The current waiver clause confirms that inaction does not constitute waiver and that any waiver must be in writing, but it omits the critical protection that a waiver of one specific breach or right does not operate as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right. Without this language, a counterparty could argue that the City of Westwood's written waiver of one instance of non-performance—for example, a missed deliverable deadline or a reporting obligation—establishes a course of conduct that extends to similar future breaches, undermining the City's ability to enforce the Agreement's terms going forward. This gap creates meaningful legal and operational exposure for the City of Westwood, particularly in a long-term professional services relationship where individual accommodations are common.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any breach or default of any provision of this Agreement shall be deemed a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or default, whether of the same or any other provision hereof.

suggestions.reason: The current clause exposes City of Westwood to three related risks. First, by identifying signatories only as "both parties" without requiring authorized representatives, a contractor could argue that a field employee's or project manager's signature or informal written communication constitutes a binding amendment. Second, the clause is silent on whether schedules and attachments are equally protected, leaving open an argument that those documents may be modified outside this process. Third, the absence of any prohibition on oral modifications or course-of-conduct amendments creates a litigation risk that a City of Westwood employee's verbal agreement or acquiescence in a changed work practice could be asserted to have amended the Agreement's terms—a risk that is particularly acute in multi-year public services contracts.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including any schedules and attachments hereto, may not be amended except by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties; no oral agreement or course of conduct shall operate as an amendment to this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 27 names only Consultant's post-termination obligations—Insurance and Indemnification—while omitting any express reference to City of Westwood's corresponding post-termination rights, such as rights with respect to intellectual property ownership, confidentiality, records retention, and audit. This asymmetry exposes City of Westwood to the risk that a court applies expressio unius to limit survival to only the two named obligations, leaving the City's key rights unenforceable after termination. Additionally, the catch-all phrase "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination" is an inherently subjective standard that two reasonable lawyers would interpret differently, creating litigation risk for City of Westwood at precisely the moment—post-termination—when enforcement of these protections is most critical.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and City of Westwood's rights with respect to intellectual property ownership, confidentiality, records retention, and audit, together with any other provisions that expressly state they survive or that by their express terms contemplate performance after termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause exposes the City of Westwood to scope and enforcement risk on two fronts. First, the enumerated components of "Accounts" (idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts, and bond proceeds) are not anchored to any investment guidelines or policy direction established by the City, leaving Consultant with unchecked discretion over the breadth of assets it manages without a corresponding obligation to follow the City's investment parameters. Second, the compliance standard "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is impermissibly vague — two reasonable lawyers would reach different conclusions about which laws are captured, creating a gap that Consultant could exploit to narrow its legal obligations and potentially dispute accountability to the City. The absence of an express fiduciary duty and the lack of reference to City-established investment guidelines further weaken the City's ability to enforce standards of conduct against Consultant.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City, including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts, and bond proceeds (collectively, the "Accounts"), in accordance with the investment guidelines established by the City from time to time. Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser with respect to the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in a fiduciary capacity on behalf of the City, and shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable federal and state laws and regulations governing investment advisers and the management of public funds.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted leaves "assets it manages" undefined, creating a material risk that the Consultant could narrowly characterize which assets fall within the scope of its fiduciary duty, thereby limiting its obligations to City of Westwood and undermining the City's intended protections. The prudent person standard is further anchored to the vague benchmark of "an enterprise of like character and with like aims," which is sufficiently indeterminate that a court could not resolve a dispute over Consultant's conduct without resort to extrinsic evidence, weakening City of Westwood's ability to enforce the standard in litigation. The clause also imposes obligations on Consultant without providing City of Westwood a corresponding express right to disclosure of conflicts of interest that could compromise the fiduciary relationship, leaving the City without a practical mechanism to identify or remediate impaired performance before harm occurs.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages on behalf of City of Westwood pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties solely in the interest of City of Westwood with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in the discharge of similar professional responsibilities, and shall promptly disclose to City of Westwood any conflict of interest or material circumstance that may impair Consultant's ability to so act.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains a typographical corruption — "Complying with Kansas the requirements" — that renders the operative sentence grammatically defective and potentially unenforceable as written, exposing the City of Westwood to a dispute over whether a binding statutory compliance obligation was ever clearly undertaken. More critically, the qualifier "where required" at the end of the clause is undefined and vague: it does not specify required by whom, under what circumstances, or by reference to which authority, allowing a counterparty to argue that the first-look obligation to local banks simply does not apply in any given transaction. For the City of Westwood, as a public entity subject to K.S.A. 12-1675 et seq., any ambiguity in whether this statutory first-look obligation is being discharged creates direct legal exposure to challenges regarding the validity of its investment transactions.
suggestions.original_text: Complying with Kansas the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675 et seq. providing local banks with a “first look” at the City’s investment opportunities where required.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Complying with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675 et seq., including providing local banks with a "first look" at the City's investment opportunities as required thereunder.

suggestions.reason: The term "periodic" imposes no defined reporting frequency, leaving the investment manager with unconstrained discretion to determine when portfolio reports are delivered to the City of Westwood. This exposes the City to material information gaps — delayed or infrequent reporting could prevent timely oversight of holdings, performance, and transactions, undermining the City's fiduciary and budgetary accountability obligations. Without an objective time anchor, the City has no contractual basis to demand reports or establish a breach if reporting lapses. This provision should be read alongside any audit rights or oversight mechanisms elsewhere in the Agreement to confirm alignment.
suggestions.original_text: Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing monthly portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance, with each report delivered no later than fifteen (15) calendar days following the end of each calendar month.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the obligation to work with the city attorney on a designating ordinance is untethered to any identifiable condition, triggering event, or specification of which of the City of Westwood's funds are in scope. The phrase "certain of the City's funds" is indeterminate, meaning the counterparty could assert the obligation arises at any time and covers any funds, exposing City of Westwood to uncontrolled engagement of this service without its affirmative direction. Without a clear trigger tied to City of Westwood's written authorization, the City also loses the ability to control the timing and scope of a legislative drafting process that carries direct legal and budgetary consequences.
suggestions.original_text: Working with the city attorney to draft an ordinance designating certain of the City’s funds as multi-year capital funds.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Working with the city attorney to draft an ordinance designating certain of the City's funds as multi-year capital funds, upon written direction from the City identifying the specific funds to be designated.

suggestions.reason: The grant of "sole discretion" to Consultant to invest City of Westwood's public funds without any prior consultation exposes the City to unchecked investment decisions affecting taxpayer assets, with no reciprocal right to be notified of or object to material deviations from agreed strategy beyond the written policy guidelines that the City must separately furnish. As a public entity with statutory stewardship obligations, the City of Westwood bears political, financial, and legal accountability for how those funds are managed, making an entirely unrestricted discretion grant commercially unjustifiable and potentially inconsistent with the City's own fiduciary duties. Additionally, "best execution" is undefined in the clause and nowhere anchored to an objective standard in the Agreement, leaving the City without a measurable benchmark against which to assess or challenge Consultant's transactional conduct. These two deficiencies together mean the City has no practical right of oversight and no enforceable performance standard for securities execution, materially impairing its ability to hold Consultant accountable.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have reasonable investment discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts; provided, however, that Consultant shall consult with the City in writing prior to implementing any material change in investment strategy, and Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, as measured against applicable regulatory requirements and industry-recognized standards, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" sets no objective standard for when the City of Westwood must deliver balances, account statements, and interest information to the Consultant, leaving the City exposed to a claim of breach based on the Consultant's subjective expectation of turnaround. Without a defined trigger and a specific period, a court or arbitrator would need to resort to extrinsic evidence to determine what performance was required, creating enforcement uncertainty at the City's expense. If the Consultant withholds or delays performance on the basis that the City failed to provide information "timely," the City has no bright-line defence. Anchoring the obligation to a written request and a fixed number of Business Days protects the City by making the condition and timeline objectively verifiable.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Within five (5) Business Days following written request by Consultant, provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "required liquidity" is undefined and carries no objective benchmark or reference standard anywhere in the Agreement, exposing the City of Westwood to a dispute in which the Consultant could assert that the City failed to supply sufficient data to "properly determine" that undefined liquidity level, thereby attributing poor investment outcomes to the City's alleged non-performance rather than to the Consultant's decisions. Without an anchor to the City's existing investment policy or operational cash flow requirements, the Consultant effectively controls the adequacy standard, shifting financial and legal risk to the City of Westwood. Anchoring "required liquidity" to the City's investment policy eliminates that ambiguity and preserves the City's ability to enforce the clause on objectively ascertainable terms.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity, as established by the City's adopted investment policy and operational cash flow requirements.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this provision requires City of Westwood to execute fund transfers across its accounts solely on the Consultant's request, with no dollar cap, no frequency limitation, and no requirement that any individual transfer be authorized by a designated City official. This exposes the City to significant financial risk: an erroneous, unauthorized, or disputed transfer instruction from the Consultant could move public funds without any independent City approval checkpoint. There is also no express limitation tying each transfer to the parameters of the Board-approved investment plan, meaning the City's compliance obligation is unbounded in scope and amount.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with reasonable advance notice, respond to Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts, subject to the City's prior written approval by an authorized City representative and solely to the extent consistent with the Board-approved investment plan.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, the City of Westwood bears an open-ended financial obligation to pay "all expenses" of securities transactions — with no cap, no reasonableness standard, and no prior approval right — based solely on confirmations unilaterally provided by Consultant directly to the Custodian. The City has no defined review window before its payment and delivery obligation is triggered, meaning the City could be bound to settle transactions and absorb unlimited transactional costs before it has had any opportunity to verify the accuracy or authority of the underlying confirmations. This structure gives Consultant unchecked power to initiate City expenditure, creating material financial and legal exposure for the City without a corresponding obligation on Consultant to provide accurate, pre-approved, or bounded confirmations.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all reasonable and documented expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, within the applicable settlement period following the City's receipt and approval of confirmations provided by Consultant, provided that such confirmations have been reviewed and approved in writing by the City prior to delivery to the Custodian.

suggestions.reason: The clause contains no contractual obligation requiring Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to the City of Westwood, which is the most critical gap: without a disclosure requirement, the City has no mechanism to identify, evaluate, or respond to a conflict before it affects its investment portfolio. Additionally, the conflict-avoidance measure is framed as Consultant's internal "policy" rather than a binding contractual obligation, meaning the City of Westwood cannot enforce it as a matter of contract if Consultant deviates. Left unaddressed, these gaps expose the City to undisclosed dual-loyalty situations where Consultant simultaneously advises an Issuer Client on bond issuance and manages the City's investments without the City's knowledge or consent.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. Consultant shall promptly disclose to the City in writing any actual or potential conflict of interest arising from its concurrent role as financial advisor to an Issuer Client and investment advisor to the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, Consultant shall not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf of an investing client or purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This obligation serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The amendment provision allows the City of Westwood to change the authorized representatives listed in Schedule X on undefined notice, creating operational uncertainty for Consultant but, more critically, the placeholder "Schedule X" renders the authorization framework incomplete and unenforceable on its face. More significantly for the City, the aggregate data right grants Consultant an unconditional, unilateral license to use Account information in its performance data without the City's prior consent, and the phrase "does not identify the City" is insufficiently precise to prevent indirect or contextual re-identification, exposing the City of Westwood to unauthorized disclosure of its financial and operational data. These deficiencies, taken together, leave the City without meaningful control over how its Account information is used externally and without a workable notice standard for authorizing amendments to the Schedule.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule [__] to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City upon not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant only with the prior written consent of the City, provided that such aggregate data does not identify, or permit the identification of, the City.

suggestions.reason: As presently drafted, the Management Fees clause exposes City of Westwood to significant financial and operational risk because it states no payment due date, provides no mechanism for City of Westwood to dispute an erroneous invoice or withhold a disputed amount without being in default, and contains no requirement that Consultant give advance written notice before changing the fee rate — leaving City of Westwood subject to unilateral fee increases mid-engagement. The absence of these protections is particularly acute given that fees are calculated by Consultant based on account balances it controls, creating an unchecked billing dynamic. No existing provision elsewhere in the Agreement appears to supply these missing payment-term protections.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant shall be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Consultant shall issue invoices within fifteen (15) days following each quarter-end, and undisputed amounts shall be due within thirty (30) days of receipt of a valid invoice. City of Westwood may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and withheld disputed amounts shall not constitute a default pending good-faith resolution. No change to the fee rate shall take effect without at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice to City of Westwood. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, and no additional expenses shall be charged without City of Westwood's prior written approval. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City of Westwood bears the entire burden of directing proxy votes while the Consultant — the engagement's investment professional — is wholly absolved of any responsibility, without even an obligation to provide proxy voting recommendations or analysis to support the City's decision-making. This creates a material operational risk for the City: as a public entity without specialist investment staff, the City may be required to cast proxy votes without professional guidance from the very party retained to manage its investment portfolio, potentially resulting in votes that harm portfolio value. The asymmetry is commercially unjustified given that the Consultant possesses the investment expertise that the City has contracted for, and the absence of any corresponding advisory obligation on the Consultant leaves the City financially exposed for consequences of uninformed voting decisions it was never adequately equipped to make.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies; provided that Consultant shall provide proxy voting recommendations to the City upon request. Consultant shall have no responsibility for the City's final direction of proxy votes.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes the City of Westwood to significant legal and financial risk because it limits Consultant's certifications solely to investment adviser registration status, with no broader warranty of compliance with applicable laws, no warranty that the Services are free of third-party intellectual property infringement, and no stated remedy if any certification proves false or is breached. Without a non-infringement warranty, the City could face claims from third parties arising from the Consultant's work product with no contractual recourse against the Consultant. The absence of an express breach remedy — such as re-performance or a fee refund — leaves the City without a clearly defined right to relief and may complicate any subsequent dispute or recovery action under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act") and shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations throughout the term of this Agreement; (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; (iv) warrants that the Services shall not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights; and (v) shall, upon breach of any warranty in this Section, at the City of Westwood's election, re-perform the affected Services or refund the fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation runs only in one direction: the Consultant certifies it is duly authorized and fully empowered, but the City of Westwood makes no corresponding representation. This asymmetry leaves the Consultant without any contractual assurance that the City of Westwood has the requisite municipal or governmental authorization to bind itself to the Agreement, which could expose both parties to enforceability challenges if the City of Westwood's authority were later disputed. More critically for the City of Westwood, the absence of a mutual representation weakens the Agreement's internal coherence and may create an argument that the clause was deliberately structured to impose a one-sided certification burden, undermining the City of Westwood's negotiating posture in any future dispute over the Agreement's validity or performance obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each Party is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
